transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62m
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Delacruz (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Liam Park (Redwood Product), Raj Patel (CTO, Zephyr), Olivia Chen (Head of Data Privacy), Marco Ruiz (ML Platform), Hannah Lee (Legal), Priya Singh (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Goal: scope a 6-8 week POC to validate latency and cost for a Zephyr in-product assistant while ensuring PII minimization and configurable prompt retention.
- Success criteria discussed: 95th pct latency under 300ms for S1 flows, cost per 1k tokens under target, zero retention for raw prompt text except via opt-in, redaction pipeline validated on sample set.
- Next: run bench, share security artifacts, schedule private deployment deep-dive.

Topics covered: success criteria, workload sizing (qps/seq-length distribution), redaction & prompt storage, retention windows, encryption/KMS, audit logs, compliance docs, timelines for POC and pilot.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about an hour. quick intros, then we'll jump into the workload and privacy constraints.
[00:14] Raj: hey, raj here, CTO at Zephyr. we built their analytics stack, and we're evaluating a lightweight assistant embedded in the product. primary concerns are PII and data residency, plus predictable latency.
[00:30] Olivia: hi, olivia, head of data privacy. we're focused on minimal retained data, redaction and the ability to prove to auditors we didn't persist sensitive fields.
[00:42] Ethan: great, thanks. quick note: i'll drive the perf/arch bits. maya will cover redaction and retention knobs, liam on product fit.
[00:55] Priya: thanks, priya here, i'll own the acceptance criteria from product side.
[01:03] (crosstalk)
[01:10] Ethan: can we start with traffic profile? marco or raj, what does expected QPS look like for the assistant on week one vs steady state?
[01:22] Marco: for the POC we're expecting small subset, roughly 15 qps peak, avg 5 qps. tokens per prompt: median 120, 95th at 420 due to long query contexts. concurrency spikes during reports.
[01:40] Ethan: ok that's helpful. we'll size the benchmark around 20 qps peak with sequence length distribution. we'll run with batching off initially to measure tail-latency, then test batching profiles.
[01:55] Raj: latency target for S1 flows is 250ms p95, but we can compromise up to 300ms if cost is favorable.
[02:06] Samira: noted. acceptance criteria so far: p95 < 300ms, no more than X dollars per 1k tokens (we'll get to cost after you share usage patterns), and redaction pipeline must remove or mask fields classed as sensitive.
[02:24] Olivia: about redaction - we need proof that original prompt text is not stored in raw form. we don't want free-text logs kept for longer than 7 days. can you do configurable retention windows per env?
[02:38] Maya: yes, Redwood supports configurable retention at per-customer level, and we have an option to retain only hashed prompt fingerprints and metadata for up to 90 days for debugging. raw prompt storage can be disabled.
[02:52] Hannah: legal question: if we disable raw prompt storage, how do we debug model regressions or escalate incidents? will you provide secure access to short-lived traces?
[03:04] Ethan: good Q. common pattern: enable short retention (e.g., 7 days) of redacted transcripts, plus ability to enable advanced logging in a VPC/private deployment where logs can ship to customer's S3 with encryption. for debug we can provide ephemeral session exports under strict audit logs.
[03:26] Olivia: and KMS? we need customer-managed keys.
[03:30] Samira: we support KMS/HSM integrations in our Private deployment and in Dedicated via bring-your-own-key for storage encryption. for hosted Tier, we have integrations with major KMS providers but we can discuss a private control plane if that's required.
[03:45] Raj: curious about redaction accuracy—are you doing rule-based? ML-based? both?
[03:51] Maya: current pattern is staged: rule-based deterministic scrubbing for phone, SSN, email, plus optional ML-based sensitive-entity detection to catch contextual PII. ML model flags go into a review queue; for the POC we recommend rule-based plus a small ML pass to measure false positives/negatives on your dataset.
[04:10] Marco: can we run that on-prem or in our VPC? we can't send raw identifiable records outside the region for the POC.
[04:18] Ethan: yep, Private deployment can sit in your VPC/region. for initial perf bench we can run in Redwood Dedicated in us-east and simulate your residency constraints, but for production validation we'd recommend a Private pilot in your region.
[04:33] (brief pause)
[04:40] Priya: for acceptance criteria we also want a weighted quality metric: model output must not hallucinate PHI into assistant replies more than 0.1% of responses on sample set. is that feasible to validate?
[04:55] Liam: we can set up a small eval harness: run 5k prompts, measure hallucination rate on labeled test set, tie alerts to regressions. Redwood Optimize can track that during POC.
[05:06] Raj: timeline check — we want a 6-week POC window with two weeks integration, two weeks benching/validation, and two weeks pilot. is that doable?
[05:16] Samira: yes that's our typical cadence. key dependency: we need your sample prompts and traffic histograms ASAP (ideally by 2026-01-18) so engineering can prep the bench.
[05:27] Marco: we'll send those. question on prompt storage — we prefer not to store user prompts by default, but we may need prompt templates and examples for fine-tuning. can those be stored encrypted with access controls?
[05:40] Maya: yes, templates and curated prompts can be stored encrypted at rest under customer-managed KMS and with RBAC in the console. raw session prompts are separate and controlled by retention policy.
[05:52] Olivia: what about logs for auditing? we need immutable audit logs that show who accessed what and when.
[05:58] Samira: Redwood Console provides audit trails for API keys, config changes, and data exports. those logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. immutable retention is configurable as part of enterprise package.
[06:10] Hannah: can you give a brief on data flows? where does raw text touch Redwood systems in hosted vs private?
[06:20] Ethan: in hosted, raw text traverses our ingress and enters a short-lived KV cache for generation; if retention is disabled it's not written to persistent storage. in Private, control plane metadata is separate and raw payloads stay in your VPC. encryption in transit and at rest always applied. note: transcriptions sometimes mis-capture K8s as kittens etc, so please excuse auto-captioning.
[06:46] (laughter)
[06:52] Priya: bench specifics — we'd like p95 and p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and an empirical chart showing caching benefit for repeated prompts.
[07:05] Ethan: we'll produce a benchmarking spreadsheet with those metrics. we'll include runs: cold start, warm with KV cache primed, and batch profiles.
[07:14] Raj: who owns remediation if redaction misses something? we need an SLA for data incidents.
[07:22] Samira: we provide incident response playbook; for Private and Dedicated we can agree on an incident SLA in contract. part of the POC we can run a redaction evaluation and include false-negatives remediation steps.
[07:36] Olivia: please add a test where we inject synthetic SSNs and emails and measure detection/obfuscation rates.
[07:44] Maya: noted, we'll run detection matrix.
[07:47] (some typing/background noise)
[07:55] Marco: regarding cost — please give both hosted and dedicated estimates. we need to understand unit economics versus our current human-in-the-loop cost.
[08:05] Liam: we'll prepare a 3-month projection for both: hosted metered vs dedicated reserved capacity assumptions. we'll call out suggestions like 8-bit quantization to reduce cost for non-critical flows.
[08:21] Raj: what about model rollbacks if quality drops? we need canary and automatic fallback to cheaper model variant.
[08:29] Ethan: built-in rollouts let you pin versions, do canary at X% traffic, and configure automatic fallback to smaller model when latency SLOs are missed. logs and metrics feed into Redwood Console for quick triage.
[08:44] Samira: quick recap: deliverables - security artifacts, bench plan, run bench w/ your samples, cost estimates, schedule private deep-dive.
[08:57] Priya: sounds good. one ask: include an explicit checkbox in the POC acceptance that raw prompts are not used for model training unless explicitly opted-in and documented.
[09:09] Maya: yes that's a standard opt-in; we can certify PII is not used for training for the POC and include it in the SOW.
[09:19] Hannah: legal will want a short addendum to the contract describing retention/incident SLA. we'll send a draft.
[09:28] Samira: great. any final questions?
[09:33] Raj: none here. thanks everyone.
[09:36] (meeting ends)

References mentioned: security whitepaper (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/whitepaper), benchmark template (sheet link shared after call), PII redaction checklist (attached in follow up), sample SOW template for POC.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker attribution occasionally generic, a few words garbled by auto-transcription (e.g., K8s -> Katies, KV -> kay-vee).

End of transcript.
